weather.tip: Overcast with a 54% chance of rain — carry an umbrella and leave early; after two days of waterlogging, expect slow stretches and avoid flooded underpasses.

around.headline: Heavy rain floods roads and uproots trees across Bengaluru
around.summary: Waterlogging and fallen trees snarled traffic on key corridors, and Bengaluru Traffic Police issued an advisory ahead of more forecast rain. Check live traffic before leaving and keep extra time for Mahadevapura-side routes.

around.headline: 19-year-old BCom student stabbed to death outside a Bengaluru college
around.summary: Reports say the student was called out of class and attacked by a group of six outside the college. Parents and students should report suspicious gatherings near campuses to 112.

around.headline: Pink Line CMRS inspection likely Oct 6–8, taking Metro past 100 km
around.summary: The 7.5-km elevated stretch between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere is moving closer to opening once safety inspection is done. Opening dates are not confirmed yet.

around.headline: Karnataka mulls licence suspension and fines up to Rs 5,000 for repeat traffic offenders
around.summary: Proposals include higher penalties, including Rs 5,000 for offences like one-way driving. They are still being considered, not yet in force.
around.source: The New Indian Express, Times of India

around.headline: Madgaon–Mangaluru Vande Bharat to be extended to Bengaluru, says Railway Minister
around.summary: The Goa–Mangaluru Vande Bharat is planned to run up to Bengaluru, and an MLC has also sought a re-routed weekend special. No start date was reported.
around.source: The Hindu, The New Indian Express

around.headline: Landlord demands Rs 4 lakh deposit for a 2BHK; another tenant told to vacate after paying deposit
around.summary: Two viral rental stories show how deposits can be abused. Get a written agreement before paying any deposit and keep payment receipts.

around.headline: Supreme Court rules out a complete firecracker ban, proposes a balanced approach
around.summary: The court is weighing public sentiment against health concerns rather than imposing a blanket ban. With Diwali ahead, expect rules on timings and types of crackers rather than a total prohibition.

street_smart.title: After heavy rain, you spot a tree branch down on a lane with a thick cable lying across the wet road, one end sparking faintly. A few people are walking past, and a two-wheeler rider is about to ride over it. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Deccan Herald / The Hindu: Bengaluru rain uproots trees and floods roads (2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01).
street_smart.situation: The road is wet, it's getting dark and nobody seems to know whether the cable is live.

choices.text: Move the cable aside with a dry wooden stick so vehicles can pass.
choices.feedback: Wet wood, wet ground and even a 'dry' stick can conduct enough current to be lethal. A sparking cable should be assumed live; a stick is no insulation.

choices.text: Step on it quickly to see if it's really live.
choices.feedback: Current flows through the wet ground around a fallen live wire (step voltage), so even near it can shock you.

choices.text: Keep everyone at least 10 m back, warn the rider, and call BESCOM (1912) and 112; stay until help arrives.
choices.feedback: You can't tell a live wire by looking. Distance plus a call to the utility gets the line switched off safely, while a warning stops the next person getting hurt.

choices.text: Take a video for social media and walk on.
choices.feedback: Posting doesn't reliably reach the utility, and the hazard stays live for the next rider or child.

takeaways: Treat any fallen wire as live, especially in water; stay 10 m away.
Never touch a person in contact with a live wire; switch off power or call for help first.

quiz.question: The Pink Line stretch likely to see CMRS inspection spans which stations?
quiz.why: CMRS (Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety) must certify a line's safety before passenger service starts.

quiz.question: What repeat-offender fine is being considered for Bengaluru-area traffic violations?
quiz.why: Proposals also include licence suspension, and these are not in force until formally notified.

quiz.question: What did the Supreme Court say about firecrackers this week?
options: It rules out a complete ban
quiz.why: Earlier court orders have favoured green crackers and time limits as a middle path.

quiz.question: Which body sets India's repo rate?
quiz.why: The MPC has six members and meets at least four times a year.

quiz.question: Which river is the main source of Bengaluru's piped drinking water?
quiz.why: Water is pumped from the Cauvery over 100 km away and lifted about 500 m uphill to the city.
